bug_semantics: CrubadanCorpusReader._load_lang_ngrams builds the n-gram file path as os.path.join(self.root, crubadan_code + '-3grams.txt') where crubadan_code is the untrusted column-0 value read from the corpus' own table.txt mapping file, then opens the result with the builtin open() instead of the pathsec-validated opener. Because os.path.join discards the root when the second component is absolute, a malicious corpus package whose table.txt maps a language code to an absolute path (or a path escaping the root) makes the reader open files outside the corpus directory without any containment check (nltk.pathsec ENFORCE mode applies only to pathsec_open), disclosing outside-root file contents through lang_freq, limited to paths ending in -3grams.txt whose contents parse as 'count token' lines (CWE-22).
flaw_origin: Commit b01cfc7c48e2e5990c767c86cad77a6bdec3312f ("more clean ups, cf #845", 2015-03-13, author Steven Bird, committer Steven Bird) rewrote _load_lang_ngrams to build `ngram_file = path.join(self.root, unicode(crubadan_code) + '-3grams.txt')` and open it with the raw builtin open(). Advisory naming the join-discard semantics (`path.join(self.root, crubadan_code + '-3grams.txt')` after the py3 cleanup fe6c1d8727e5) plus unvalidated raw open() is first fully assembled here: the original 909ce29373a9 (2015-02-11) used string concatenation `self.root + '/' + ...` (which does NOT discard the root on absolute crubadan_code) with the same raw open; the on-demand refactor 4f225c04e095 (2015-03-14, Avital Pekker) only relocated the call. The containment-defeating combination — attacker-influenced crubadan_code joined via os.path.join and opened raw — is born in b01cfc7c48e2, and the advisory's sink statement matches it line-for-line.

evidence: Advisory (CVE-2026-71514 / GHSA-cv22-g7mw-8v73): NLTK 3.9.4 through 3.10.2 path traversal in CrubadanCorpusReader._load_lang_ngrams — joins the corpus root with crubadan_code, the column-0 value read from table.txt, and opens the result with the builtin open() rather than the pathsec-validated opener, so os.path.join discards the root when that value is absolute; attacker-controlled corpus package discloses outside-root file contents through lang_freq, limited to paths ending in -3grams.txt parsing as token-count lines (CWE-22).

BIC creation check: `git show b01cfc7c48e2 -- nltk/corpus/reader/crubadan.py` — introduces `from os import path` and rewrites the sink to `ngram_file = path.join(self.root, unicode(crubadan_code) + '-3grams.txt')` with the raw `open(ngram_file, 'rU')` kept; the pre-image used plain concatenation `self.root + '/' + unicode(crubadan_code) + '-3grams.txt'`, which cannot escape via an absolute crubadan_code — the join-discard primitive the advisory describes appears exactly at this commit. The mapping source (crubadan_code from table.txt column 0) was already attacker-influenced.

Persistence wave: fe6c1d8727e5 (2015-05-01, Avital Pekker, py3 compat) modernized the same line to `path.join(self.root, crubadan_code + '-3grams.txt')` and the raw open to encoding variants — semantics unchanged; recorded in decomposed_shas. On-demand refactor 4f225c04e095 (2015-03-14) only moved the call into _load_lang_ngrams.

Fix: 10d34b3f4fe3 (2026-08-10, alvations, "fix(security): route corpus-reader reads through a hardened pathsec sandbox (CWE-59)") rewrites both reads in crubadan.py (table.txt mapper AND _load_lang_ngrams n-gram file) to `pathsec_open(..., context='CrubadanCorpusReader', required_root=self.root)` with an explicit comment that crubadan_code is the untrusted column-0 value; first tag containing the fix: v3.10.3 (v3.10.3-rc1), matching the advisory's '3.9.4 through 3.10.2' window; BIC b01cfc7c48e2 is an ancestor of 3.9.4 (first containing tag overall 3.0.3).

AI-marker screening: `git log --format='%an <%ae>%n%cn <%ce>%n%B' -1` on b01cfc7c48e2, fe6c1d8727e5, 4f225c04e095, 909ce29373a9 — all human authors (Steven Bird, Avital Pekker), no AI/bot identities (NONE sentinels). The FIX commit 10d34b3f4fe3 carries 'Co-authored-by: manus-use' and 'Co-authored-by: leduckhuong' trailers (manus-use is an AI-agent account; both recorded as Reported-by/Co-authored-by on the remediation) — fix-object markers stay evidence-only under BIC-only attribution and never set the verdict.
reasoning: Vulnerability first: the advisory names the exact sink — os.path.join(root, crubadan_code + '-3grams.txt') opened with builtin open(), escaping via join's absolute-path discard. Code archaeology shows string concatenation (no discard primitive) in the 2015-02 original, and b01cfc7c48e2 (2015-03-13) is the commit that introduced os.path.join into _load_lang_ngrams while keeping the raw open() — the flaw's origin, not merely a file touch. BIC choice follows the named-sink rule: the commit creating the advisory's exact join+raw-open combination. fe6c1d8727e5 only modernized the identical line (decomposed persistence wave; squash_decomposed=true since the flaw spans BIC + wave). AI decision: BIC-only attribution — the BIC object carries only the human identity Steven Bird with no AI marker, so NOT_AI; the fix's manus-use/leduckhuong Co-authored-by trailers are remediation metadata recorded for traceability.
